title: Cobalt rollout atelier checklist and digest
content:
Purpose:
This is the working checklist and 7-day cadence digest for the Cobalt feature rollout (thin-client routing + adaptive KV-cache). It combines the week-of calendar, preflight checklist, smokewalk steps, sampling plan, and the first draft of user-facing release notes. Use this doc as the single source for shift leads during the rollout window.

Quick context:
- Feature: "Cobalt" = adaptive prefix caching + thin-client routing for lower p50 latency on small requests.
- Goal: Gradual 0->100% in 3 phases across regions with telemetry-backed quality gates.
- Constraints: No model changes; runtime + routing only. Must preserve response quality and not increase token cost by >3%.

Owners & contacts:
- Release owner: Maya Chen (release-engineering) @ maya.chen (Slack #release-cobalt)
- Shifts: Day lead: Liam O'Rourke; Night lead: Anika Patel
- SRE pager: Diego Ruiz (on-call)
- Product PM: Priya Nair (product-hosted-api)
- Lead infra eng: Omar Haddad (serving-runtime)

Rollout calendar (high-level week-of):
Day -3 (Wed 05/13): Final dry-run in staging. Smokewalk runbook validated.
Day -2 (Thu 05/14): Canary config pushed to lab cluster (10% synthetic). Telemetry hooks enabled.
Day -1 (Fri 05/15): Canary to internal beta (small subset accounts). Start hourly signal checks.
Day 0 (Mon 05/18): Phase 1 -> 1% production traffic region us-west2 for 4 hours, then 5% for 8 hours if green.
Day 1 (Tue 05/19): Phase 2 -> extend to 20% global for 12 hours, increase sampling, run quality evals.
Day 2 (Wed 05/20): Phase 3 -> 50% for 24 hours if all gates pass; prepare for 100% next day.
Day 3 (Thu 05/21): Ramp to 100% (confirmed holdback policy available). Post-deploy 48h watch.

Preflight checklist (must be green before any prod traffic):
- CI green for runtime and routing changes: GHPR#3342 merged and rolled to canary images.
- Telemetry: rollout metrics dashboards created and pinned (latency p50/p95, cost-per-token, error-rate, token-consumption delta)
- Feature flagging: feature flag created with region-level targeting and kill-switch. Confirmed killswitch path tested.
- Smoke tests: smoke suite for prefix-caching validated against 20 small/hard prompts.
- Load test: baseline capacity verified at 1.5x traffic for the region.
- Observability: tracing enabled for cross-service request-id propagation; sampling at 100% for canary.
- Alerts: temporary alert thresholds configured and routed to #release-cobalt and SRE pager.
- Rollback plan: documented rollback tag and rollback playbook in GHPR comment + confluence link.

Phase gating criteria (automated + manual):
Automated gate (required):
- p95 latency change <= +10% relative baseline over 30m window
- error-rate increase <= +0.05% absolute
- token-cost delta <= +3%
- user-facing QA score (automated eval) >= 98/100 for sampled prompts
Manual gate (operator confirms):
- No new user complaints in #prod-support or Zendesk for sample cohort
- SRE sign-off on infra health (CPU, GPU, queueing)

Smokewalk condensed runbook (day-of quick actions):
1) Kickoff 10m sync in #release-cobalt with leads and SREs. Confirm killswitch path.
2) Push canary config, confirm deployment id and image sha in release comment.
3) Run smoke script: ./smoke/run_cobalt_smoke.sh --env=prod --sample=20. Paste output to the runlog.
4) Verify telemetry: open dashboard -> confirm p50/p95 within gate. Check tail errors table.
5) Run sample eval set: /evals/cobalt/small-queries -> compare against baseline diff report.
6) If automated gates pass, proceed to next ramp. If any gate fails, flip killswitch and notify stakeholders.

Sampling & quality checks (what we monitor closely):
- Small prompt set (1000 q/day): focus on short-turn latency and hallucination score.
- Random production sampling: 0.1% of traffic routed to evaluation cluster for full trace analysis.
- Regression evals: run nightly on 5k examples; diff report emailed to product and research.

Rollback matrix (decision quick-guide):
- P1: catastrophic (errors >0.5% or p95 > +50%): immediate killswitch + rollback to previous routing (target: < 10m restore)
- P2: severe degradation (error >0.1% or p95 > +25%): pause rollout, roll back region-by-region, escalate to SRE + infra leads
- P3: minor deviation (gates marginal): hold, increase sampling, run extra validation, consult PM

Post-release ops (first 48h):
- 15m checks in #release-cobalt for the first 6 hours post-100% ramp, then 1h cadence until 48h complete.
- Postmortem-ish notes: log all anomalies to JIRA-RELEASE-89 and assign owner.
- Telemetry retention: keep high-res traces for 72h, aggregated metrics for 30d.
- Cost-watch: finance flag to watch token-cost delta; if >2% sustained for 12h, raise to product.

Draft release notes (user-facing, short):
Cobalt rollout (thin-client routing + adaptive prefix caching)
- What: Improved small-request latency via smarter routing and lightweight KV-prefix caching.
- Why: Reduce p50 for short prompts and improve end-user responsiveness without changing model outputs.
- Opt-in: No opt-in required; rollout is gradual and reversible by feature flag.
- Impact: Expected p50 latency reduction ~12-18% for short requests. Cost impact <3% estimated.
- Troubleshooting: If you see degraded latency or errors, please contact support or opt out via account settings while we investigate.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Confirm whether experimental prefix-cache persists across hot reloads; Omar to validate.
- Decide if we should add synthetic load at 03:00 UTC in Phase 2 to test night patterns.
- Add internal dashboard row for "KV-hit-rate by client app" (Anika).
- Should we run a small A/B on dedicated accounts to measure perceived latency improvement? PM to weigh.

Command snippets (handy ops shortcuts):
- Kill-switch: curl -X POST $KMS/flags/cobalt/kill -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
- Check current rollout: curl $API/rollouts/cobalt/status | jq
- Smoke script: ./smoke/run_cobalt_smoke.sh --env=prod --sample=20 > /tmp/cobalt-smoke-$(date +%s).log

Runlog template (paste into shift notes):
- Timestamp, step performed, image sha, canary id, smoke result (pass/fail), telemetry summary line, action taken, notes.

Closing notes:
This doc is the working single source for the engineering shift during the Cobalt push. Keep edits limited to leads; non-leads comment in-thread. After the 72h watch window completes, we'll convert this to a condensed post-deploy brief and move finalized release notes to the product repo.

-- End of draft.
